correctness.rationale: Direct Brandt multiplication forces every commuting off-diagonal family to have disjoint source/target sets. In any inclusion-maximal family all allowed off-diagonal group labels and rectangle edges are saturated and the complementary diagonals are maximal abelian subgroups; the converse is maximal and closed. The generating polynomial and total count follow from unique parametrization and inclusion-exclusion. The maximum uses the sharp rectangular product inequality and checks n=1,2,3 separately. The Gaussian law is a multinomial central limit with exponentially rare conditioning and bounded O(n) diagonal error; variance 2p^3(1-2p). Direct checker exhausts ten independent examples, including nonabelian S3, and prints VERIFY_OK. General proof does not depend on finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: The specific claim is all maximal commutative subsemigroups inside each fixed Brandt B_n(G), a weighted cardinality polynomial using actual maximal abelian subgroups, and a Gaussian typical-size law. Abstract group-plus-annihilator form already known is credited. Historical-equivalence risk is explicitly retained.

value.rationale: The full finite size spectrum of maximal commutative subsemigroups is a natural semigroup invariant. The classification reveals how the actual maximal abelian subgroups of a fixed nonabelian G control it, and the Gaussian law gives typical quadratic-size behavior distinct from sharp extremal size. This is a complete motivated structural/enumerative result, not an arbitrary small-case computation or a renaming of the known abstract divisor decomposition.
